## The two traps that are specifically yours

**1. Identity of the room row** (risk 6, and the one most likely to bite). `loadRoom` writes: a `wrapping` room with no fresh recording seat becomes `wrapped` on read, and the handler after it sees the mutated row via `Object.assign(collab, done)`. `loadRoom` must hand back **the same `collab` object it mutated** — never a spread copy, never a rebuilt literal. A copy gives `info` the pre-wrap phase, and no type error will tell you. `loadRoom` returns `Promise<Response | Room>` and the dispatcher checks `instanceof Response`.

The temptation to tidy this is the single most likely way this PR stops being a pure move.

Also still true from the earlier passes: ordering is behaviour (the wrap on read happens before `wrapDeadline` and `roomExpired` are computed); flat files with `.ts` extensions; `import type` for `Caller`, `Room` and `Sql`; no `deno.json`; static imports only; no new file named `index.ts`; only `index.ts` calls `Deno.serve`; predicates stay imported from `_shared/collab.mjs`.
